headline: GOLD SLIDES TO $4,357, SILVER TO $64.69 AS IRAN SECOND WAVE AMPLIFIES OIL SHOCK — September FOMC Rate-Hike Odds Spike To 70% As Safe-Haven Logic Inverts
snippet: Gold fell to $4,357/oz and silver to $64.69 on September 2 as a second wave of U.S. military strikes on Iranian targets — met with Iranian retaliation against U.S. bases in the Middle East — paradoxically pressured precious metals rather than triggering a safe-haven surge. The mechanism: oil back above $90/bbl driven by Strait of Hormuz tensions is adding to the inflation picture, which bond markets are now pricing as additional rate-hike fuel. September FOMC hike odds have spiked to 70% — up from 40% just a week ago — while the 10-year Treasury yield hit 4.79%, its highest since January 2025, sharpening the opportunity cost of holding non-yielding bullion. Gold December futures opened at $4,377.20 before sliding further through morning trading. The inversion of the typical war/gold correlation is a function of the specific 2026 macro regime: sustained conflict at $90+ oil breaks the disinflation narrative before it breaks the economy, and history suggests that when this regime eventually reverses, it does so sharply.

headline: SOUTHERN CROSS GOLD HITS 972 g/t AU OVER 0.6m AT 808 METRES DEPTH — Apollo East Extended To Easternmost Limit As Sunday Creek High-Grade Persists Below 800m
snippet: Southern Cross Gold Consolidated Ltd (TSX: SXGC / ASX: SX2) released September 2 results from five drill holes at its Sunday Creek Gold-Antimony Project in Victoria, Australia, including the 9th best composite intersection in Sunday Creek drilling history: 0.6 metres at 972.0 g/t Au and 8.9% Sb (993.2 g/t AuEq) from 808.5 metres vertical depth — 620 metres below surface. The release also documents the furthest eastern extension drilled to date at Sunday Creek, systematically increasing the project's resource footprint. The result ranks among the highest-grade underground gold intercepts reported globally in 2026, and its position at 808 metres depth demonstrates that Apollo's bonanza-grade ore persists well beyond depths typical for Victorian-era gold workings. At gold above $4,300/oz, ultra-high-grade narrow-vein underground economics at Sunday Creek are among the most compelling in the junior sector.

headline: AZTEC MINERALS EXTENDS TOMBSTONE STRIKE TO 1,250m — 83.8 Metres At 1.31 g/t AuEq In Arizona Oxide System; Maiden Resource Estimate Approaching As 93-Hole Program Nears Completion
snippet: Aztec Minerals Corp. (TSXV: AZT) announced September 2 that drilling has extended the Contention gold-silver system at its Tombstone Property in southeastern Arizona to more than 1,250 metres of continuously drilled strike — adding 255 metres to the previously defined footprint. Results from five reverse circulation holes include TR26-41's 83.8 metres of 0.90 g/t Au and 22.61 g/t Ag (1.31 g/t AuEq), including a 7.6-metre high-grade core of 6.97 g/t Au and 75.42 g/t Ag (8.34 g/t AuEq). With 93 RC holes completed in the 2025-2026 program and assays pending on nine more holes, Tombstone is approaching the data density required for a maiden mineral resource estimate — a milestone that will formally quantify one of Arizona's most consistent oxide gold-silver discoveries for the first time. Tombstone's shallow, oxide mineralisation profile is well-suited to heap leach processing in a jurisdiction with developed mining infrastructure.

headline: WALLBRIDGE FENELON PFS DRILLING: 52.30 g/t AU OVER 2.1m — 635-kg Bulk Sample Averages 5.00 g/t As Quebec Gold Project Advances To Pre-Feasibility Study
snippet: Wallbridge Mining Company Limited (TSX: WM) published September 2 the final assay results from seven holes drilled as part of its 2026 Pre-Feasibility Study metallurgical program at the Fenelon Gold Project in northern Quebec. Intercepts include 52.30 g/t Au over 2.1 metres, 25.41 g/t Au over 3.6 metres, and 8.27 g/t Au over 16.4 metres. The seven holes collectively yielded 635 kilograms of mineralized material averaging 5.00 g/t Au for metallurgical variability testing — approximately 20% above the minimum sample mass required — while an additional 185 kg at 6.92 g/t Au came from zones peripheral to the current resource. Fenelon's grade profile, demonstrated here from a genuinely representative bulk sample, positions the project favourably against most active gold PFS processes in Canada. Results feed directly into the ongoing Pre-Feasibility Study, the document that will define capital costs, mining method, and ultimately the investment decision.

headline: PALADIN ENERGY'S PLS ATLAS ZONE: 17.5m AT 1.75% U3O8 — New High-Grade Uranium Results Expand Saskatchewan's Patterson Lake South District Beyond Triple R
snippet: PLS Exploration — a joint venture including Paladin Energy Ltd (ASX: PDN / TSX: PDN) — released September 2 new high-grade uranium results from the Atlas discovery at the Patterson Lake South project in Saskatchewan's Athabasca Basin, including a 17.5-metre composite interval averaging 1.75% U3O8. The Atlas body is a new corridor discovered during winter 2026 drilling that expands the PLS district beyond the existing Triple R resource of over 73 million pounds U3O8. With NexGen's Rook I under construction next door and uranium spot hovering around $89-90/lb, additional high-grade exploration success at PLS directly increases the probability of a district-scale, multi-deposit development scenario in one of the world's premier uranium-bearing basins. Paladin used its September 2 Investor Day to present the Atlas results alongside progress on its Langer Heinrich restart in Namibia.

headline: GOLD MINERS' NEAR-RECORD Q2: $10.9B IN 2026 DIVIDENDS AND BUYBACKS — Agnico Eagle's $1.3B Free Cash Flow Quarter Shows Producers Are Outpacing Bullion By Design
snippet: GoldSeek's analysis of Q2 2026 earnings across senior and mid-tier gold producers documents near-record fundamental performance driven by gold averaging above $4,000/oz through the quarter. Agnico Eagle (TSX: AEM) led with record free cash flow of US$1.3 billion, record cash on hand of US$3.5 billion, and a credit rating upgrade to A- from Fitch — while the broader senior producer universe is tracking US$10.9 billion in annualized dividends and share repurchases, putting 2024-2026 on pace to return more capital than the preceding 13 years combined. For junior mining investors, the implication is direct: majors and mid-tiers flush with record cash are active buyers of discovery-stage assets with clear resource growth trajectories, and the premium for drill-bit momentum in safe jurisdictions is likely to widen into Q4 as M&A speculation builds toward year-end.

headline: DOLLAR CONCERNS STRENGTHEN GOLD'S STRUCTURAL CASE — GoldSeek SWOT: Palladium Best-Performing PM Of The Week (+5.30%) On South African And Russian Supply Constraints
snippet: GoldSeek's weekly Gold SWOT analysis for the week ending August 31 identifies dollar deterioration as the structural tailwind most likely to sustain gold's bull market beyond the current Fed rate-hike overhang, arguing that prolonged dollar weakness tied to U.S. fiscal trajectory overrides rate differentials on a 12-24 month horizon. The analysis notes palladium was the week's best-performing precious metal, gaining 5.30%, driven by persistent supply constraints from both South Africa — where Q1 2026 output fell 26% year-over-year at Norilsk Nickel and production costs are rising — and Russia, where geopolitical sanctions continue to redirect supply flows. For investors in PGM-adjacent junior miners, the Pd and Pt supply-constraint story is fundamentally separate from the gold debasement narrative but reinforces the broader case for precious and critical metals exposure.

headline: CHINA RARE EARTH STANDDOWN EXPIRES NOVEMBER 10 — CSIS: U.S. Imports Never Recovered To 2024 Levels Despite Suspension; Pentagon Backs Domestic REE Race As Deadline Looms
snippet: A CSIS analysis marking approximately one year of China's rare earth and magnet export control regime finds that despite the October 2025 measures being suspended until November 10, 2026 — under the APEC Busan stand-down agreement — U.S. imports of Chinese rare earths have still not recovered to pre-restriction 2024 levels, while European supply chains have partially adapted. The November 10 review deadline is now weeks away, with Beijing expected to assess whether to reimpose, escalate, or further extend the controls. U.S. companies report greater disruption than European peers. The Pentagon has responded by accelerating support for domestic rare earth production, including MP Materials' Apple supply agreement (valued at US$500 million) and USA Rare Earth's Oklahoma magnet manufacturing facility targeting defense, EV, and clean energy markets — but the gap between Western dependency and genuine self-sufficiency remains years wide regardless of November's outcome.

headline: PLATINUM'S 297,000-OZ 2026 DEFICIT GOES UNPRICED — WPIC: South Africa, Russia, Zimbabwe Control 90% Of Supply As Nornickel Output Falls 14-16% And Fuel Cell Demand Accelerates
snippet: The World Platinum Investment Council's 2026 market update projects a 297,000-ounce platinum deficit — driven by South African mine production declining toward 3.695 million ounces (down from 3.820 Moz in 2025) as electricity constraints and rising costs persist, and Norilsk Nickel's H1 2026 platinum output falling 26% year-over-year with palladium down 18%. South Africa, Russia, and Zimbabwe collectively control approximately 90% of primary platinum supply — a geographic concentration more extreme than almost any other critical commodity, and one that magnifies geopolitical and operational supply risks. Despite the structural deficit, platinum remains historically undervalued relative to gold. Demand from hydrogen fuel cell vehicles and industrial catalysts is growing secularly, while primary supply is in structural decline from all three major producing regions simultaneously.

headline: ALGO GRANDE COPPER CLOSES OVERSUBSCRIBED $4.79M PLACEMENT FOR ADELITA DRILLING — Sonora, Mexico Copper Explorer Raises Capital As $6.59/lb Copper Spurs Junior Funding Revival
snippet: Algo Grande Copper Corp. (TSXV: ALGR) closed a non-brokered private placement on September 1, raising $4,786,498 through the sale of 7,977,497 shares at $0.60 each — oversubscribed, signalling active investor demand for junior copper exposure. Proceeds fund ongoing drilling and exploration at the 100%-owned Adelita Project in Sonora, Mexico, one of the most copper-prolific states in North America. The oversubscribed close is notable context: with copper above $6.59/lb ($14,500/tonne) and three of the world's four largest copper mines simultaneously underperforming, junior copper explorers with drill programs in established mining districts are attracting institutional and family office capital that was largely absent from the sector two years ago. Sonora's established mining infrastructure, water access, and processing options make it a practical jurisdiction for development-stage copper projects.
